notes: Runnable: with deepseek-flash for every role, a readiness smoke completes two accepted dev rounds (round 2 frozen) and hidden test_001 Result 89 (scoreable), independent review 10/10, gate READY with source_unchanged; the release-provenance formal gate dry run passes.

Release change (2026-10-10): Docker 29 removes an exited or stopped --rm container asynchronously: for several seconds `docker inspect` still shows it and `docker rm -f` answers "removal of container ... is already in progress" (exit 1); Docker 24 has removed it by then. harbor/formal_one_stop.py remove_and_verify_broker records rm's stderr and, when rm answers "already in progress" (an --rm broker that exited by itself), waits up to 30 s for the container to be gone before deciding absent_after_cleanup. Any other rm refusal is judged as before, and a container still present after the wait is not absent. Seen with Docker 29.2.1.

Release change (2026-10-10): harbor/formal_one_stop.py exits 0 for a complete readiness smoke. Under a readiness binding the acceptance finalizer is skipped on purpose (the readiness judge smoke is the single judge evidence), but the exit status still required finalizer_exit == 0, so every complete, valid smoke exited 2 and `agentswe status` showed the unit as failed. A readiness smoke now succeeds when its hidden execution is complete, nothing in it is infrastructure-invalid and its readiness judge smoke completed; pilot and formal exit logic is unchanged. Scores are unaffected.
